To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed and expressed a core capsid protein fusion with EGFP at the C- terminus, assembled it into VLPs and determined its crystal structure.
a recombinant hepatitis B virus core protein dimer linked to EGFP was designed, expressed in E. coli, purified, crystallized and its X-ray structure solved to 2.2 Å resolution.
we have expressed, purified and crystallized the hepatitis B virus core protein fusion to EGFP.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structural characterization of a recombinant hepatitis B virus core protein fusion, which may be useful for the development of a vaccine against hepatitis B. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a major global health problem.
a new approach to the production of hepatitis B virus capsids for use in vaccine development.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a new crystal form of the hepatitis B virus core protein, which is a novel octahedral VLP with a unique structure.
a fusion core protein, CPD-EGFP, has been expressed and crystallized, which will provide an excellent platform for further studies of the hepatitis B virus assembly process.
the fusion CPD was crystallized in an octahedral lattice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CPD-EGFP fusion proteins can be assembled into both icosahedral and octahedral particles and the octahedral particles can be used for structural studies.
the fusion protein was designed, expressed, purified, crystallized and the crystal structure was solved to 2.2 Å.
the crystal packing of CPD-EGFP fusion protein was driven by the octahedral symmetry of the protein assembly, rather than the intrinsic symmetry of the fusion protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a CPD fusion protein can be expressed, purified, assembled and crystallized in a manner similar to that for the native core protein.
the fusion CPD protein can be used as a model system for the study of hepatitis B virus capsid assembly and disassembly.
the fusion CPD is able to assemble into VLPs and that the crystal structure of the VLP will provide a better understanding of the mechanism of capsid formation.
